title: TileSet.create_tile() sorting after each tile causes compounding lag as TileSet grows
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf
- Present in source from at least 4.4-stable through 4.7-stable

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Intel Core i9-14900KF (32 threads), 62 GB RAM - Godot 4.7.2.stable, GL Compatibility, headless

### Issue description

**Note:** Cleaned up, hand written, non-AI version of #123445 as per rules.

**The Issue**

Large tileset images with many tiles lag both the game and editor when they're created and loaded. This appears to be caused by a sorting function that causes more lag the more tiles are added as it's performed after each individual tile is added to the map.

**How it was discovered**

I was testing a number of premade tilesets I'd bought off itch.io and one of them (Modern Exteriors) had an all-in-one tileset image that had everything in it (about 56K tiles). When adding the image I was prompted if I wanted all non transparent tiles set up, I hit yes and the editor lagged heavily for several minutes before completing the task, however while the tileset was visible the editor was extremely slow to the point of almost being unusable. Having it in "TileMap" mode when placing tiles, the lag didn't exist.

I found after adding some tiles to a board and booting up the game moving from one board that had a small tileset to the big one, caused minutes of load were the game would just lock up. My machine is a fair monster and can run ray-traced nonsense so I was surprised that a 7MB 2D tileset image was causing this much strain.

I wasn't sure what to do with this as whilst it was a big tileset, I refused to believe it was beyond what games were capable of, again a 7mb image is teenie tiny and ~56K rows isn't catastrophic in the grand scheme of things.

I tested having the same 56k tiles split up into separate smaller tilesets, but still all included in the same board, vastly increased load time, which was odd.

| Sources | Tiles each | Load | Speedup |
|--------:|-----------:|------:|--------:|
| 1 | 56,639 | 41.51 s | — |
| 2 | 28,320 | 20.41 s | 2.03× |
| 4 | 14,160 | 10.03 s | 4.14× |
| 8 | 7,080 | 4.99 s | 8.32× |
| 16 | 3,540 | 2.54 s | 16.33× |
| 32 | 1,770 | 1.34 s | 31.06× |

**The Cause**

With some help from that which will not be named, the problem was traced to `scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp:5014`

```
// Create and resize the tile.
tiles.insert(p_atlas_coords, tad);
tiles_ids.push_back(p_atlas_coords);
tiles_ids.sort();          // full re-sort, once per tile

_create_coords_mapping_cache(p_atlas_coords);
_queue_update_padded_texture();
```

Effectively the more tiles in a single tileset, the more the lag compounds as every single tile added resorts the entire set on a single thread so whether in editor or game, loading the resource causes massive slowdown.

**Suggested Fix**

I don't have one myself but the clanker ticket suggested lazy sorting and a dirty flag instead of sorting eagerly.

**Workaround**

Split the same tileset image into smaller tileset instances, you can use all of them on the same board without the slowdown but having all 56k etc. tiles on one tileset causes the issue.

### Steps to reproduce

For this I'm copying over the code from my original ticket as it's purely a test script reference.

The same can reproduced by manually creating tilesets of different sizes from a large image and measuring the load time.

Worth noting the issue is caused by source size not image size so dividing one big image into many tilesets is fine.

Run with `godot --headless --path <project> --script res://repro.gd`

```gdscript
extends SceneTree


## Times TileSetAtlasSource.create_tile() as the tile count grows
func _initialize() -> void:
	for tile_target: int in [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]:
		# Build an empty atlas source over a placeholder texture
		var texture := PlaceholderTexture2D.new()
		texture.size = Vector2(2816, 8224)
		var source := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
		source.texture = texture
		source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
		source.use_texture_padding = false

		# Create tiles one at a time, as the resource loader does
		var started_usec: int = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		var created: int = 0
		for y: int in 514:
			for x: int in 176:
				source.create_tile(Vector2i(x, y))
				created += 1
				if created >= tile_target:
					break
			if created >= tile_target:
				break
		var elapsed_usec: int = Time.get_ticks_usec() - started_usec

		print("%6d tiles: %8.3f s" % [created, elapsed_usec / 1000000.0])
	quit()
```

| Tiles | Time | × previous |
|------:|------:|-----------:|
| 1,000 | 0.008 s | — |
| 2,000 | 0.036 s | 4.50 |
| 4,000 | 0.164 s | 4.55 |
| 8,000 | 0.714 s | 4.35 |
| 16,000 | 3.020 s | 4.23 |
| 32,000 | 12.632 s | 4.18 |

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - See single script above, paste-able into any project. I imagine I can't redistribute the exact tileset I'm using here.
